question: What is the meaning of environmental contamination in relation to chemical and biological properties?
description: Environmental contamination refers to the presence of harmful substances in the environment, which can be chemical or biological in nature. These contaminants can negatively impact ecosystems, human health, and the overall quality of the environment. The text mentions substances of concern, including carcinogenic, mutagenic, toxic to reproduction, endocrine disruptors, toxic to specific organ targets, sensitive for respiration and skin, persistent, bioaccumulative, and toxic (PBT), and very persistent and very bioaccumulative (vPvB). These substances pose risks to the environment and living organisms, highlighting the importance of tracking and managing environmental contamination.
